---
name: chatgpt-artist-getting-started
description: Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the ChatGPT Artist bot.
---
# ChatGPT Artist: getting started

Ask one thing at a time, with tappable choices wherever you can. Wait for the answer, confirm it in one line, then move on. The owner never writes a prompt; you write every one. Follow `chatgpt-image-studio` for images and `codex-cloud-helper` for coding.

1. **Hello.** One or two lines: you turn their ideas into finished images using their own ChatGPT account, and you can hand coding jobs to Codex Cloud if they want. Nothing gets posted anywhere without their yes.
2. **What do you want to make?** Choices: Characters/creatures, Posters/covers, Logos/brand art, Memes/stickers, Photo-style scenes, Something else. Save the answer as their default focus.
3. **Connect images.** Choices: **Sign in with ChatGPT (recommended)**, or Use an OpenAI API key instead.
   - ChatGPT: open chatgpt.com in your box browser. If it's already signed in, confirm the account and plan. If not, follow the `sign-in` skill: the owner signs in through the handoff, typing their own email, password and 2FA. You never ask for or type their credentials. Confirm you can see a new-chat composer, and note their plan if it's shown (Free plans have tighter image limits).
   - API key: request it through the masked secret form as `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and never let them paste it in chat. Check it with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.openai.com/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY"` (expect 200). Tell them the API bills per image, separately from their ChatGPT plan.
4. **Bring your style.** Ask: Do you have a signature style ChatGPT already knows? Choices: Yes, it has a name; Yes, it's in a file (like AGENTS.md); No, help me find one later. To import one, follow the Saved styles section of `chatgpt-image-studio`, then show them a 3-line summary and save the style.
5. **Coding too?** Choices: Yes, set up Codex Cloud; Not now. Only if they say yes, run the setup in `codex-cloud-helper` (it needs Plus or higher and a GitHub repo). Otherwise skip it and offer it later.
6. **First image, right now.** Run `chatgpt-image-studio` with short choice questions (subject, style, mood, shape). Show the result and offer: Love it, Variation, Change something.
7. **Wrap up.** Tell them in one line what they can ask for next ("make a poster in my style", "fix my website"). Save their connection choice, focus, and saved style names to memory.

---
name: chatgpt-image-studio
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants an image made, varied, or edited from an idea,
  however vague, through their ChatGPT account or OpenAI API key, or wants to
  save or use a named art style.
---
# ChatGPT image studio

The owner answers choices and you write the prompt. Never publish, post, or share anything without their yes.

## Saved styles
The owner's named styles live in `~/chatgpt-artist-styles/<Name>.md`, each one a paste-ready style block. Offer them first in the Style question.
- **Import from ChatGPT:** a computerUse subagent opens a new chat in the signed-in box browser and sends: "Describe my <Name> art style in full detail, using everything you know about it from my memory and past chats. Cover subject matter, line work, rendering/shading, color palette, lighting, texture, composition, mood, influences, typography, what to avoid, and recurring motifs. Then write it as a reusable style block I can paste in front of any image prompt. If you don't actually have a <Name> style saved, say so plainly instead of inventing one." Have it copy the full reply verbatim. Save the style block plus any palette and avoid rules to the style file, and keep the chat URL as the source. If ChatGPT says it has no such style, tell the owner and don't make one up.
- **Import from a file:** if the style is in an `AGENTS.md` or a doc on the owner's computer, find it with their approval, pull out the style section, and save it the same way.
- **Using a style:** on the API and Codex routes, put the full style block at the front of the prompt. On the ChatGPT route, also say "in my <Name> style" so ChatGPT's memory reinforces it. For Codex work, point the repo's `AGENTS.md` at the style file so the coding agent reads it too.

## 1. Gather (one question at a time, tappable choices)
- **Subject**: offer 3-4 guesses based on their idea, plus "Something else".
- **Style**: their saved styles first, then Photoreal, 3D render, Anime/cartoon, Oil/watercolor, Flat vector, Pixel art.
- **Mood/lighting**: Bright and cheerful, Dark and moody, Dreamy, Epic/cinematic, Minimal. Skip this when a saved style already sets the mood.
- **Shape**: Square 1:1, Tall 9:16 (phone/story), Wide 16:9, Portrait 2:3, Landscape 3:2.
- **Reference image?** Yes, I'll send one; No. If yes, ask whether it should keep the person/object, the style, or both.
- **Text in the image?** None (the default), or Yes, and get the exact words.
Skip anything that's already clear, and ask 5 questions at most.

## 2. Build the prompt
Write one paragraph covering subject and action, setting, style, mood and lighting, camera and composition, aspect ratio, and either the exact text in quotes or "no text". Put the saved style block in front if one was picked. Show a one-line summary ("Here's what I'll ask for: ...") with choices Go and Tweak.

## 3. Generate
**ChatGPT route (default).** A computerUse subagent uses the box browser, already signed in at chatgpt.com. It starts a new chat, attaches any reference image, pastes the prompt, sends it, and waits for the image to finish. Then it saves the image into `~/chatgpt-artist-out/`, using the image's download button or by opening the image and saving it. If the session has signed out, run the sign-in handoff again and never type credentials. If ChatGPT says an image limit was reached, tell the owner when it resets (as shown on the page) and offer the API route if a key is set. Unverified: OpenAI doesn't publish exact per-plan image limits, so report what the page says.

**API route (when `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set and the owner chose it).** Docs: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation
```bash
curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-image-2.5-sunburst","prompt":"<PROMPT>","size":"1024x1536","quality":"high","n":1}' \
  | jq -r '.data[0].b64_json' | base64 -d > ~/chatgpt-artist-out/<name>.png
```
To edit an image or use references (several `image[]` files are allowed):
```bash
curl -s https://api.openai.com/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_API_KEY" \
  -F model=gpt-image-2.5-sunburst -F "image[]=@ref1.png" -F "image[]=@ref2.png" \
  -F "prompt=<PROMPT>" -F size=1024x1024 | jq -r '.data[0].b64_json' | base64 -d > out.png
```
Sizes: 1:1 is `1024x1024` (or `2048x2048`), 9:16 is `1152x2048`, 16:9 is `2048x1152`, 2:3 is `1024x1536`, and 3:2 is `1536x1024`; `auto` also works. Custom sizes need both sides in multiples of 16, a ratio between 1:3 and 3:1, and a longest side of 3840 at most. Use `gpt-image-2.5-flare` for fast drafts. `gpt-image-1` was shut down on Oct 23, 2026.

## 4. Show and iterate
Send the image file with choices: Love it, 3 variations, Change something (then ask what: colors, pose, background, text, or style), Different shape. If they approved a composition, keep it and change only what they asked for. For edits, work from the last image: on ChatGPT, ask in the same chat; on the API, call `/images/edits` with it as `image[]`. Keep the final file and its prompt in `~/chatgpt-artist-out/`.

skills.content:
---
name: codex-cloud-helper
description: >-
  Use when the owner wants coding work done on a GitHub repo through Codex Cloud
  (OpenAI's cloud coding agent), or asks to set up, check, or apply a Codex
  task.
---
# Codex Cloud helper

The owner may not code. Ask plain questions, write the task yourself, and explain results in plain words. Never merge, push, or open a pull request without their explicit yes.

## 1. Requirements (say them plainly)
- A ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise or Edu plan. Free and Go don't include Codex Cloud, and cloud tasks share the plan's usage limits.
- A GitHub account connected at chatgpt.com/codex, plus a published cloud **environment** for the repo.

## 2. CLI install and sign-in (ask before installing)
```bash
command -v codex || npm install -g @openai/codex   # or: curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh
codex login status        # exit 0 = signed in
codex login --device-auth # default: ChatGPT sign-in on a headless box
```
Device auth prints a URL and a one-time code. Send both to the owner; they open the link on their own device, sign in, and enter the code. You never handle their password.
API key backup, only if they chose it (the key is stored as `OPENAI_API_KEY` through the masked secret form): `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key`. Unverified: whether Codex Cloud tasks work with API-key sign-in, so assume they need ChatGPT sign-in.

## 3. Environment check
Run `codex cloud list --json`, or plain `codex cloud`, which opens an interactive picker that lists environments. If no environment exists, walk them through setting one up step by step: open chatgpt.com/codex, connect GitHub, pick the repo, then create and publish the environment. You can do this in the box browser once they've signed in through the sign-in handoff. Note the environment ID.

## 4. Write the task
Ask one question at a time, with choices: which repo/environment; what's wrong or wanted (fix a bug, add a feature, change text/design, explain the code); and how they'll know it worked. Then write a scoped task: the goal, the files or area if known, acceptance criteria, and "keep changes minimal, add or update tests, don't touch unrelated code". If the owner has saved art styles that the work needs (UI art, game assets), make sure the repo's `AGENTS.md` points to the style file. Show the task in one line and get a yes.

## 5. Submit and track
```bash
codex cloud exec --env <ENV_ID> "<TASK>"           # add --attempts 2-4 for best-of-N
codex cloud list --env <ENV_ID> --json --limit 5   # id, url, title, status, summary
```
Check the status until it's done, and share the task URL so they can watch at chatgpt.com/codex.

## 6. Report and apply
Summarize the result in plain words: what changed, which files, and any risks. Give them choices:
- Looks good, make a PR: they do it, or you click "Create PR" on the task page only after their yes.
- Change something: send a follow-up on the task.
- Apply locally: run `codex apply <TASK_ID>` inside a clone (it exits non-zero on conflicts).
- Discard.
Never push or merge yourself.
Ref: https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli/reference
